key_idea: By linearity of expectation the answer is sum of v_i * area(disc of radius r around plant i intersected with the garden) / (w*h); the circle-rectangle intersection area has a closed form.
sketch: For each plant, shift so it is the origin and integrate over x in [max(-r,-x), min(r,w-x)] the vertical extent min(h-y,s(t)) + min(y,s(t)) with s(t)=sqrt(r^2-t^2). Each term is piecewise: constant c where |t| < sqrt(r^2-c^2), and s(t) outside, whose antiderivative is (t*s + r^2*asin(t/r))/2. Sum the pieces exactly in long double, O(n) total. Pitfalls: 1e-9 tolerance rules out sampling or coarse numeric integration, clamp the asin argument and the sqrt radicand, and handle c >= r (no clipping) separately. Checked against fine midpoint integration on random cases.
